forces.title: Elevated financing costs hinder construction investment
forces.description: Higher interest rates and financing costs across Europe are making households and businesses more cautious about investing in new property. This directly impacts residential and non-residential building construction, leading to subdued growth and slower recovery, thereby constraining demand for building products. New builds are particularly affected as buyers often finance payments during construction.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Geopolitical risks and energy price volatility escalate costs
forces.description: The Middle East conflict and other geopolitical uncertainties are increasing energy prices and causing supply chain disruptions, notably impacting transport costs and raw material availability. This leads to higher production costs for energy-intensive building materials and components, making it harder for manufacturers to pass costs through and potentially delaying projects due to buyer reluctance.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Residential building sector remains a weak spot
forces.description: The residential construction market across Europe, including new housing permits, has stabilized or seen declines in many regions (France, Norway, Netherlands). High construction costs and lower affordability, coupled with buyer reluctance due to uncertainty, make new projects less commercially viable. This directly reduces demand for building components and systems targeting new home construction.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Infrastructure and defense spending bolster construction demand
forces.description: Increased investment in infrastructure, including energy and digital networks, railway expansion, and defense spending, is providing an important offset to construction headwinds across Europe. These projects drive demand for building components and systems like pipes, fittings, and specialized building automation, particularly for commercial infrastructure and data centers, supporting sector activity.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Demand for energy-efficient homes drives specific product sales
forces.description: Rising energy prices and increasingly stringent renovation requirements are widening the value gap between energy-efficient and energy-intensive homes. This boosts demand for investments in insulation, high-performance glazing, and more efficient heating systems. For building product manufacturers, this creates a resilient demand segment for energy-efficient HVAC, building automation, and other sustainable components.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Staff shortages constrain construction project delivery
forces.description: Staff shortages in the construction sector across Ireland and the Netherlands are limiting project execution and contributing to delays. This constraint on overall construction activity impacts the uptake of building products, as project completion rates are hindered, potentially leading to reduced and delayed orders for component manufacturers.

forces.title: Data center buildout fuels demand for specialized components
forces.description: Data center capacity in Europe is projected to double or triple by 2030, driven by AI and cloud computing. This rapid expansion creates significant demand for fabricated components, including prefabricated structures, electrical enclosures, racks, and cooling components (HVAC). This represents a high-growth segment for building product manufacturers specializing in these areas.
forces.source_title: The next wave of value in the materials supply chain

forces.title: AI to redefine AEC workflows, impacting building products
forces.description: The integration of AI and automation into the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry is expected to significantly improve efficiency and consistency in design, planning, and site execution. This structural change will drive demand for building products that are easier to manufacture, transport, install, and inspect, and those compatible with smart, automated building systems and digital twins.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: Investment shifts to existing facilities, energy efficiency, digitalization
forces.description: Capital investment in the Irish health sector (and broadly in construction) is prioritizing improving existing facilities through refurbishment, energy efficiency upgrades, and administrative digitalization, rather than new build expansion. This trend, driven by construction cost inflation and regulatory constraints, creates sustained demand for modern building components, smart systems (building automation), and energy-saving solutions for existing structures.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Supply chain resilience becomes competitive advantage
forces.description: Global volatility and disruptions (Brexit, Covid-19, Ukraine, Middle East) have made supply chain visibility, resilience, and agility strategic imperatives for Irish manufacturing, including building products. Firms are proactively identifying choke points, implementing mitigating actions like dual supply, and leveraging digital/AI tools to strengthen supply chains, which influences sourcing decisions and demand for domestically produced or regionally sourced components.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Strong competition from Asian manufacturers in domestic market
forces.description: Norwegian manufacturing contacts report strong international competition, particularly from Asian manufacturers. This dampens expectations for domestically oriented firms, including those in the building products sector. This external competitive pressure can lead to margin erosion and market share loss for European manufacturers if not addressed through differentiation or cost efficiency.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

viewpoints.title: Europe's construction sector to experience weak, subdued growth
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects EU construction output to grow marginally by 0.5% in 2026, following a 1.8% decline in 2024. While infrastructure investment and Germany's rebound provide some support, high financing costs, geopolitical risks, and weakness in the residential building sector cap overall momentum. This subdued growth implies limited demand expansion for building products manufacturers.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Dutch construction stabilizing, modest growth expected in 2027
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts the Dutch construction sector to stabilize in 2026 with zero growth, recovering to a modest 1% growth in 2027. This recovery is primarily driven by an increase in building permits gradually translating into housing construction. However, the overall recovery remains limited, influenced by high construction costs, staff shortages, and nitrogen restrictions, suggesting a slow demand improvement for building products.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing faces challenging outlook but energy-efficient demand resilient
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market shows resilience in Q2 2026 but is expected to cool, with nominal price growth slowing to 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027 due to weak mortgage lending and higher interest rates. However, demand for energy-efficient homes remains resilient, driven by higher energy prices and stricter renovation standards, offering a specific growth segment for building products like insulation and efficient HVAC systems.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Irish construction strengthening with broad-based growth, but housing weak
viewpoints.description: Ireland's construction activity continues to strengthen with sustained new order inflows, benefiting commercial and civil engineering. While housing remains the weakest segment due to policy constraints, underlying demand is strong for the longer term. Key risks include cost inflation, staff shortages, and delivery delays. This suggests a positive demand trend for building product manufacturers outside of residential.

viewpoints.title: Norwegian construction remains low with delayed residential upturn
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's contacts indicate that Norwegian construction activity remains low, with few new residential and commercial projects. The anticipated upturn in residential construction is continually delayed, and profitability is weak amid fierce competition. However, state-level projects and data center buildout offer some offsetting growth drivers, suggesting a challenging but segmented market for building product suppliers.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: AI poised to unlock significant value in European construction sector
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that AI and automation technologies could unlock approximately $126 billion in annual value in the European construction sector by 2030. This transformation involves redesigning workflows, improving data use, and automating work sites, promising increased efficiency and consistency. For building product manufacturers, this implies a potential demand shift towards smart, modular, and easily integrated components that align with AI-driven design and execution.
viewpoints.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

demand_drivers.description: AI and automation streamline design, modeling, and construction-feasibility workflows, improving consistency and reducing nonphysical work, ultimately driving overall sector value.

new_opportunities.description: Demand for smart, modular, and easily integrated building components and systems that support AI-driven design, automated site execution, and long-term building maintenance/diagnostics.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected annual value unlock for the European construction sector through AI and other automation technologies.
